calculate_potential.name: Calculate the potential
calculate_potential.description: Replays the history of each vehicle with other ways of charging and compares the monthly peak, the demand charge and how often the car would not have been ready. Read-only, an estimate. Administrators only.

create_dashboard.name: Create the dashboard
create_dashboard.description: Builds the Plugwhen dashboard with the entities of this installation and returns it as YAML, to paste into a new dashboard. An existing dashboard is never changed. Administrators only.

send_feedback.name: Send feedback

data.name: Name
data.soc_max_age_h: Maximum age of the state of charge

data_description.odometer_entity: Sensor with the odometer (km or miles). It needs long-term statistics (a state class), that is where Plugwhen learns from.
data_description.soc_entity: Sensor with the state of charge of the battery in percent.
data_description.soc_max_age_h: An older state of charge counts as unknown: no plan, no warning. While charging, 90 minutes without a new value already count as stale. 0 = no limit.
data_description.reserve_km: The car should leave with at least this range. You can change it later with the Reserve entity.
data_description.consumption_kwh_100: Used until the car's own consumption is known (typical: 15 to 25 kWh per 100 km).
data_description.charge_kw_max: What the wallbox can deliver at most. The plan never plans more.
data_description.charge_kw_min: Lowest charging power of the wallbox (1 phase, 6 A is about 1.4 kW).
data_description.charge_kw_pref: The plan does not spread the charging flatter than this value, because the car loses more at very low power. Default 4 kW.
data_description.plugged_entity: On when the car is plugged in. Needed for the warning "plug in".
data_description.charging_entity: On while the car is charging. No warning is sent while it charges.
data_description.wallbox_energy_entity: Energy counter of the wallbox (Wh or kWh). It tells charging at home from charging away.
data_description.more_wallbox_energy_entities: If the car also charges at other wallboxes, enter their energy counters here. Plugwhen finds out by itself which one it is charging at. If two cars share a wallbox, enter it for both: they are then never planned at the same time.
data_description.departure_entity: A time or date-time entity (for example a helper). If set, it replaces the departure Plugwhen has learned.
data_description.notify_service: One or more notify services, separated by commas, for example notify.mobile_app_phone, notify.mobile_app_tablet. Used for the warning that the car will not be ready. Leave empty for none.
data_description.notify_hour: The warning is sent from this hour of the evening on, once per departure.
data_description.evcc_vehicle: Then plugged in and charging come from evcc as long as no sensor is set for them. Odometer and state of charge stay the car's own sensors.
data_description.trip_calendar: Every event is a trip: start = departure, kilometres in the title (“Linz 200 km”) or from the location, there and back unless it says “one way”. All-day events are ignored.
data_description.stock_soc: Plugwhen never plans below this, so the car is ready for an unplanned trip too. 0 = off.

finish.title: May I ask a favour?
finish.description:
Anonymous data helps me improve Plugwhen, and helps you at the start: while your car is still learning, Plugwhen uses the consumption of the same car models.

**Sent:** once a week an overview of the set-up with an id that changes every month; daily trip, charging and parked days without date, place or id.
**Never:** names, addresses, places or passwords.
**For:** consumption values per car model, seeing which devices work well, and summaries that are published or passed on to research and partners. Always from at least 10 installations, never single cars or households.
**Deleting:** weekly data when you switch off, otherwise after 60 days. Trip days cannot be traced to a car and therefore cannot be deleted.

All details: aiwhatelse.eu/datenschutz. Voluntary, and you can switch it off any time. Thank you!

init.title: Connections
init.description: Optional. Plugwhen also works alone. Connect it with what you have.

data.use_solar_forecast: Use the solar forecast of the Energy dashboard
data.price_low: Demand charge per kW and year
data.route_waze: Kilometres of calendar trips via Waze
data.direct_early: Offer “direct” before the learn mode is through

data_description.waechter_entry: Choose the quarter-hour peak guard and Plugwhen finds its load forecast by itself (and keeps the charging under its peak target). Suggested automatically if exactly one is installed.
data_description.load_entity: Only for another source: a sensor with the attributes hours (t, typical, high) and target_kw. Not needed when you chose the peak guard.
data_description.availability_entity: A sensor with the attributes schema (1), valid_until and forecast (a list of start, end, kw), for example from an energy community or a solar forecast.
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Optional. With an outdoor temperature Plugwhen plans a cold morning with more energy. Empty: taken from the Wächter.
data_description.weather_entity: Optional: the temperature expected at departure. Empty: taken from the Wächter.
data_description.use_solar_forecast: Charge with the expected solar surplus first, spread the rest. Uses the solar forecast of the Energy dashboard.
data_description.solar_deduct_kw: kW taken off the solar forecast first, for what the house and a home battery use. Empty: learned from the night-time base load of the grid import counter (default 0.5 kW until then).
data_description.grid_energy_entity: For the potential calculator: the meter's import counter (Wh or kWh, with long-term statistics). Taken from the quarter-hour peak guard if it is chosen.
data_description.price_low: For the potential calculator, in your currency per kW and year (up to the threshold). Empty: taken from the peak guard, otherwise only kW are shown.
data_description.price_high: Price per kW and year above the threshold. Empty: the same price.
data_description.price_threshold: kW from which the higher price applies. 0 = one price.
data_description.evcc_url: Only if you use evcc and the Wächter does not know it already, for example http://192.168.1.20:7070. Empty = the address from the Wächter.
data_description.evcc_password: Only if evcc asks for one.
data_description.route_waze: For events without kilometres Plugwhen works out the route with the integration Waze Travel Time. For this the destination goes to OpenStreetMap, home and destination go to Waze. Kilometres in the event always come first.
data_description.direct_early: For trying it out: “direct” can be chosen although “ready to switch” is not green yet.
data_description.waze_hint: Kilometres of calendar trips via Waze: add the integration “Waze Travel Time” once (no account), then the switch appears here.
